## During the seminar

We will connect histogram areas and kernel smoothing to last week's concept
of density. Repeated samples let us study a statistic as another random
variable and distinguish sample size from simulation repetitions.

The LLN describes concentration of sample means, while the CLT describes
their standardized limiting shape. We will compare simulated cumulative
probabilities with a Normal approximation, including a repeat with a
different seed. Squared deviations and estimated standard errors motivate
the chi-squared and t distributions.

Demo 8b explains the functions, lists, and CDF comparison used in A4.
Demo 11 computes the t statistic from each sample and compares two-sided
tail probabilities. The F and unbiasedness previews are optional.

## After class

**A4 is due October 14 at 1:30 p.m. Pacific.** Accept your private repository
invitation and follow its README. Complete the R answers file and QMD, then
commit and push both source files and the freshly rendered HTML.

When exploring the demo, change n and B separately. Explain which change
alters the sampling distribution and which changes the simulation's precision.
Use the probability comparisons alongside the plots, not as a claim that
every aspect of the distribution is Normal.
